overview: The John H. Chafee program gives states federal money to help foster youth move into adulthood, including education and training vouchers that help pay for college or job training. This bill raises the maximum voucher from $5,000 to $12,000 a year. It lets states give a grace period so a young person can keep receiving help after an assessment shows good reason, such as a temporary break from school. States would have to make reasonable efforts to tell eligible youth about the vouchers and offer a simple, standard application form available online, and could use program funds for that outreach. The Department of Health and Human Services would issue model guidance, and the changes would take effect one year after enactment. As of May 7, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say the current $5,000 cap covers only a small share of today's college costs, and a larger voucher plus simpler applications would help more foster youth finish school.
against: Critics say raising the per-student amount without increasing the program's overall funding could mean fewer young people receive vouchers.
